name: La Reine Marlene - SIA Project 23 24
description: La Reine Marlene is a company specialized in the sale of home materials and products. The information system manages relationships with suppliers, product proposals, supplier orders, incoming goods, inventory and replenishment, physical and online purchases, deliveries, customer support, and business statistics. Suppliers submit proposals that are evaluated by the administration department. Goods are verified when they arrive at stores. Inventory is monitored and automatic replenishment can be configured. Customers can purchase products online, pay through multiple methods, and track deliveries. Support requests are managed through tickets with automatic assignment, response deadlines and reassignment mechanisms. Company management can analyze data concerning orders, sales, inventory and customer support.
rawDescription: La Reine Marlene is a company specialized in the sale of home materials and products. The information system manages relationships with suppliers, product proposals, supplier orders, incoming goods, inventory and replenishment, physical and online purchases, deliveries, customer support, and business statistics. Suppliers submit proposals that are evaluated by the administration department. Goods are verified when they arrive at stores. Inventory is monitored and automatic replenishment can be configured. Customers can purchase products online, pay through multiple methods, and track deliveries. Support requests are managed through tickets with automatic assignment, response deadlines and reassignment mechanisms. Company management can analyze data concerning orders, sales, inventory and customer support.
highLevelGoals: The Supplier aims to easily and effectively submit their product offerings to La Reine Marlene for consideration.
The Supplier seeks assurance that their submitted product proposals are properly evaluated and have a fair chance of being accepted.
The Administrator aims to thoroughly assess and select the most suitable product proposals from suppliers to ensure quality and market relevance.
The Administrator seeks to ensure the information system is correctly configured and operates efficiently to support all business processes.
The Warehouse Staff aims to precisely check and confirm the details of all incoming goods against orders to prevent discrepancies.
The Warehouse Staff seeks to keep precise records of all products in stock to ensure availability and prevent stockouts or overstocking.
The Warehouse Staff aims to automatically or manually trigger and manage the replenishment of products to maintain optimal stock levels.
The Customer aims to easily browse, select, and buy desired products through the online platform.
The Customer seeks to make payments for their online purchases using various secure methods without concerns about data security.
The Customer aims to monitor the real-time status and expected delivery time of their purchased items.
The Customer Support Agent aims to effectively receive, categorize, and process customer inquiries and issues through a ticketing system.
The Customer Support Agent seeks to resolve customer problems within defined deadlines, potentially through automatic assignment and reassignment mechanisms.
The Manager aims to access and analyze detailed data on orders, sales, inventory, and customer support to understand overall business performance.
The Manager seeks to leverage business statistics to identify trends, evaluate performance, and guide strategic planning and operational adjustments.
The Store Clerk aims to quickly and accurately handle customer transactions for products bought directly in the physical store.
The Store Clerk seeks to correctly process various payment methods for immediate sales made by customers in the store.
lowLevelGoals: The Supplier interacts with the system to create and submit a new product proposal, including all necessary details.
The Supplier uploads images associated with a specific product proposal to enhance its presentation.
The Supplier modifies the details of a previously submitted or pending product proposal.
The Supplier checks the current evaluation status of their submitted product proposals.
The Supplier receives automated notifications regarding changes in the evaluation status of their product proposals.
The Supplier views detailed feedback provided by the Administrator on their submitted product proposals.
The Supplier formally accepts the terms and conditions for a product proposal that has been approved by the Administrator.
The Administrator retrieves a comprehensive list of all submitted product proposals, with options to filter by status.
The Administrator accesses the complete details of a specific product proposal for thorough review.
The Administrator changes the status of a product proposal (e.g., 'Approved', 'Rejected') and provides relevant feedback.
The Administrator sends a request to the Supplier for additional information or clarification regarding a specific product proposal.
The Administrator updates specific system-wide parameters, such as tax rates or shipping rules, to maintain optimal operation.
The Administrator assigns or modifies roles and permissions for different users within the system.
The Administrator edits the content and structure of automated system notifications, such as order confirmations.
The Administrator accesses detailed logs of system activities for monitoring, auditing, and troubleshooting purposes.
The Warehouse Staff uses a scanner to record the arrival of a new shipment, initiating the verification process.
The Warehouse Staff fetches the details of a specific purchase order to compare against incoming goods.
The Warehouse Staff logs the exact quantity of a specific item received against a purchase order.
The Warehouse Staff documents any differences between the expected and actual quantities of received items.
The Warehouse Staff marks an entire shipment as fully received and verified after all items have been checked.
The Warehouse Staff adjusts the quantity of a specific product in stock due to receipt, sale, or other inventory changes.
The Warehouse Staff records the physical count of a product in a specific storage location to verify system accuracy.
The Warehouse Staff moves a specified quantity of a product from one storage location to another within the warehouse.
The Warehouse Staff retrieves the real-time quantity of a specific product currently in stock.
The Warehouse Staff flags a quantity of a product as damaged, removing it from available inventory.
The Warehouse Staff accesses a list of products that have fallen below their predefined reorder point.
The Warehouse Staff creates a request to purchase more of a specific product to replenish stock.
The Warehouse Staff approves a generated purchase requisition, allowing it to proceed to the purchasing department.
The Warehouse Staff monitors the current status of an ongoing replenishment order from a supplier.
The Warehouse Staff defines the minimum stock level for a product that triggers a replenishment alert.
The Customer searches and filters products available on the online platform using categories or keywords.
The Customer accesses comprehensive details, specifications, and images for a specific product.
The Customer adds a specified quantity of a product to their online shopping cart.
The Customer modifies the quantity of an item that is already present in their shopping cart.
The Customer deletes a specific item from their online shopping cart.
The Customer initiates the checkout process from their shopping cart to finalize a purchase.
The Customer chooses an existing shipping address or enters a new one for their order.
The Customer chooses their preferred payment method (e.g., credit card, digital wallet) for the online purchase.
The Customer inputs the necessary information for the selected payment method to complete the transaction.
The Customer enters and applies a promotional or discount code to their order during checkout.
The Customer authorizes and finalizes the payment for their online order.
The Customer receives a notification confirming the successful processing of their payment.
The Customer accesses a list of all their past and current online orders.
The Customer retrieves the current processing and shipping status of a particular order.
The Customer sees estimated delivery dates and tracking numbers for their purchased items.
The Customer gets alerts when the status of their order delivery changes (e.g., 'Shipped', 'Out for Delivery').
The Customer Support Agent accesses a list of newly submitted customer support tickets, with filtering options.
The Customer Support Agent takes ownership of an unassigned support ticket to begin processing it.
The Customer Support Agent changes the status of a support ticket (e.g., 'Open', 'In Progress', 'Resolved').
The Customer Support Agent adds internal notes or comments to a support ticket for documentation or collaboration.
The Customer Support Agent assigns a category or tag to a support ticket for better organization and routing.
The Customer Support Agent filters and views support tickets based on their assigned priority level.
The Customer Support Agent marks a ticket for escalation to a higher-level support agent or manager due to complexity or urgency.
The Customer Support Agent sends a direct message or update to the customer regarding their support ticket.
The Customer Support Agent marks a support ticket as resolved and provides details of the resolution.
The Customer Support Agent transfers a support ticket to another customer support agent for handling.
The Manager creates a report detailing sales performance over a specified date range and product category.
The Manager accesses a report showing current inventory levels, including items with low stock.
The Manager obtains statistics on customer support performance, such as average resolution time and ticket volume.
The Manager exports specific business data (e.g., sales, inventory) into a CSV format for external analysis.
The Manager accesses a high-level summary dashboard displaying key business metrics and performance indicators.
The Manager compares sales data between two different time periods to identify trends and changes.
The Manager generates a list of the best-selling products within a specified timeframe to inform purchasing and marketing strategies.
The Manager reviews aggregated customer feedback to identify common issues, sentiments, and areas for improvement.
The Manager uses historical data to predict future inventory requirements for specific product categories.
The Manager assesses the effectiveness of a specific marketing campaign based on sales data and other relevant metrics.
The Store Clerk adds a product to the current in-store transaction by scanning its barcode.
The Store Clerk finds and adds a product to the current transaction by searching its name in the system.
The Store Clerk modifies the quantity of an item already added to the current in-store transaction.
The Store Clerk removes a specific item from the current in-store transaction.
The Store Clerk applies a discount to a specific item within the current in-store transaction.
The Store Clerk computes the final total amount due for the current in-store transaction, including taxes and discounts.
The Store Clerk records a cash payment received for an in-store transaction and calculates change.
The Store Clerk initiates and processes a credit or debit card payment for an in-store transaction.
The Store Clerk applies a gift card as a payment method for an in-store transaction.
The Store Clerk prints or emails a receipt for a completed in-store transaction.
The Store Clerk processes a product return, initiating a refund or store credit based on the original transaction.

baselineCritiques.actors: The identified actors are comprehensive and accurately reflect the roles described in the software description. The inclusion of "Store Clerk" is appropriate given the mention of "physical... purchases," distinguishing them from online customers. The "Administrator" and "Manager" roles are distinct and align with the administrative and analytical functions described. No significant omissions or contradictions were found.
baselineCritiques.highLevelGoals: The provided high-level goals are comprehensive and accurately reflect the functional requirements described in the software description. They cover all key actors (Supplier, Administrator, Warehouse Staff, Customer, Customer Support Agent, Manager, Store Clerk) and their respective responsibilities (proposals, evaluation, inventory, online/in-store sales, support, analytics). The goals are functional in nature, focusing on the 'what' and 'why' of the system's capabilities without delving into technical implementation details. There are no contradictions with the description, and no significant functional areas appear to be omitted.
baselineCritiques.lowLevelGoals: The low-level goals are comprehensive, well-structured, and accurately reflect the functional requirements derived from the high-level goals and software description. The coverage of all major business processes (proposals, inventory, online/in-store sales, support, analytics) is complete and consistent with the provided high-level goals.
